name: Basa, ruBasa / Basa-Benue, formerly Bassa-Kwomu

catalog_citation: Blench, Roger M., with Paul Imoh & Robert Hyslop. 2019. A dictionary of the Basa language with an English-Basa reverse. Trial edition, unpublished manuscript (PDF 'Basa Dictionary 2019 ', created 1 Jan 2019), 41 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. the Internet Archive 20250528200256 ofhttps://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Kainji/Basa/Basa%20Dictionary%202019%[Glottolog hh 569153]
catalog_locator: Front matter p. ii, section 'Tones'; CV-structure remark p. i, section 'Basa or Bassa?'
catalog_quote: Like most Nigerian languages, Basa is a tone language and important distinctions of meaning are based on tones. This section explains the tone-system briefly and the marks used to indicate tone. Tones fall on vowels and nasal consonants. There are five possible tones, three level tones and two glides, rising and falling. These latter are rare and they could be analysed as combinations of level tones. The tones are shown over the letter to which they apply as follows; [table: High ʹ / Mid Unmarked / Low ˋ / Rising ˇ / Falling ˆ] When words are different only in tone, they are listed in the order low, middle, high. ... Maɲ distinctions of meaning are made in Basa through tones. In some cases these are grammatical. For example; [table: Present / Past: 'to say' hiɛn / hiɛ́n; or; Imperative / Past: to return guré / gurè] In other cases, the meaning of words is different according to the tone. For example; [table: to wear úrúgónó / to cover ùrùgono]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Basa-Benue is described as a tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) plus rare rising and falling contours, carrying both lexical and grammatical contrasts; the source says nothing about word stress or accent (no statement of its presence, absence or position).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; contour tones said to be rare and analysable as level-tone sequences.
new_statements.domain_note: Orthography/dictionary front matter for ruBasa (Basa-Benue, Kogi State, data collected at Edenye 1991); word-level tone marking of citation forms. The 'technical appendix' on the sound system announced on p. i is not present in the 41-page PDF.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources describe Basa-Benue (ruBasa, formerly Bassa-Kwomu/Bassa-Komo), the Kogi/Nasarawa/FCT variety of the Basa cluster, which is the reference variety of Glottolog basa1282 [bzw]; Blench's dictionary data were collected at Edenye (Kogi State) in 1991 with Paul Imoh. Not to be confused with Basa-Gurmana/Kɔrɔmba [separate Glottolog entry], Nupoid Bassa-Nge, Cameroonian Basaa [bas] or Liberian Bassa [bsq].
